insight: Nyla's brand is a closed room at 2am — and the Berlin listeners just proved that room has an audience on the other side of the world without her having to shout.
guidance: Hold the stillness. The Berlin spike happened because the music was quiet and specific, not because it was loud. Everything this week should reinforce that restraint: one voice, low light, no performance of 'making it.'
voice_rules: Write like you're texting one person you trust, not broadcasting to a feed
No exclamation points, no 'y'all,' no manufactured hype — ever
Short sentences. Space between thoughts. Let things breathe.
Ask real questions when you engage — not 'thoughts?' but something you'd actually want to know
Reference specific things: a time of night, a city, a line from the song — not generic emotion
visual_rules: One light source: warm lamp or candle, never overhead or ring-light
Muted palette: deep blues, warm amber, near-black — nothing bright or saturated
Still camera or slow movement only — no jump cuts, no trending transitions
Face or hands in frame, not full-body performance shots
Grain is good. Lo-fi feels honest. Polished feels false for this brand.
avoid: Any graphic announcing stream counts, milestones, or 'we hit X' — breaks the intimacy immediately
Trending audio that isn't hers — her sound is the point, not the trend
Over-explaining the music in captions — let the song do the work, captions add texture not summaries
Posting in bright daylight with high saturation — wrong time of day for her world
